title: Where is my Ion? Correlative STEM and APT Analysis of Low-Dose Magnetic Ion Implantation in Ferroelectric Materials
content: Ion implantation is a key technique in semiconductor and quantum technologies, enabling control over nanoscale material engineering such as precise control over magnetism, the formation of solid state qubits, and the integration of sensors and emitters. This talk highlights the importance of correlative atomic-scale structural analysis using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging and electron diffraction techniques like 4D-STEM, combined with high-sensitivity, three-dimensional (3D) chemical mapping through atom probe tomography (APT). These techniques provide a comprehensive understanding of nanoscale modifications in materials, particularly in the context of ion implantation and multiferroic behaviour.
